title: Building brighter futures one school welcome at a time
summary: For the third year, Entergy Arkansas employees started the school year with high fives, smiles and a warm welcome for students across the state.
body_markdown:
For the third year, Entergy Arkansas employees started the school year with high fives, smiles and a warm welcome for students across the state.


Through Next Generation Arkansas, Entergy Arkansas is investing not only in the power system but in the people and communities that make the state stronger. Team members visited more than 50 schools, greeting students as they arrived for the day and helping make the start of a new school year a little brighter.


“It’s very important to be out in the community, to give back to the communities that we serve and deliver power to every day,” said Jarrod Harris, Entergy Arkansas customer service manager.


Employees, including lineworkers who serve these same communities, spent the mornings meeting students, offering encouragement and having a little fun along the way.


“It’s getting some high fives, greeting kids, making sure we start them off on the right note,” said Harlan Jones, journeyman lineman. “Hopefully it starts their day off as good as it starts ours.”


Journeyman Lineman Ramsey Williams said the experience is a great way to give back and connect with the people they power.


“It’s always fun coming to the schools, making kids laugh and have a good morning,” Williams said. “It’s just joyful giving back to the community and the kids.”


This year, Entergy Arkansas is also extending its support beyond the morning welcomes by providing grants to 27 schools across the state. Schools can use the funding to support classroom supplies, programs or other initiatives that meet their individual needs.


“Just giving this small token can go a long way to show them that we are here for the community and we serve this community in more ways than one,” Harris said.


For employees, the visits are just as meaningful as they are fun.


“It’s an awesome moment, a proud moment and makes me enjoy my job even more seeing these students get out of the car and they are excited to see us,” Harris said.


From supporting local schools to creating opportunities for students and families, the company is committed to helping build a brighter future for the next generation of Arkansans.
